Examined base_text units of provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift lines 1189-2413. These lines are unchanged in this PR. The range map is complete, and its changes sit at base 3444-3499 and head 3444-3727. That changed region is the write-behind big-donation admission test, refactored to use production bounds (SSDPrefixCachePolicy.writeQueueMaxJobs and productionQueuedByteCap). It is outside these units.

The visible tests cover T-041 posture:
- Epoch is not rotated by eviction, TTL sweep or corrupt-drop (1223-1321).
- A binding change wipes the root and disowns the superseded cache (1323-1366).
- Absent blocks are distinguished from corruption (1378-1430).
- Reconciliation does not follow symlinks (1544-1572).
- TTL telemetry ignores invalid drops (1617-1654).
- Write cap drops donations before extraction (1656-1704).
- Ready receipts are suppressed on failure (1787-1865).
- Write-behind enforces durable barriers and the free-space reserve (1988-2104).
- Staging reservations are released (2323-2413).

These are test-only and add no production attack surface. They are consistent with the T-041 mitigations: the TTL, the disk budget, the 20 GiB reserve including the pending payload, no-follow I/O and reservation release paths.

No regression was identified. The changed head test (3685-3727) and the production SSDWriteBehind/SSDPrefixCachePolicy sources were not supplied in these units. Integration should confirm whether the PR changes the production queue bounds (writeQueueMaxJobs, writeQueueMaxBytes or slack). That matters to T-041's bounded host-Data/no-memory-carve posture. A test refactor alone does not weaken controls.
